vision_features.image_context: A human hand (palm facing up, with a gray ring on one finger) is holding approximately 12–15 small, round seeds, each roughly 6–8 mm in diameter. The seeds appear to be soybean seeds. The plant organs visible are seeds only.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Purple-to-dark-violet discoloration patches: Located on the seed coat surface of multiple seeds (approximately 6–8 out of the ~13 seeds visible). The discoloration ranges from deep purple to dark violet-blue and covers anywhere from a small spot (~2–3 mm) to nearly the entire seed surface on the most affected seeds. The patches are irregular in shape, with diffuse, blending edges rather than sharp borders. No distinct halo or contrasting margin around the colored areas. The texture of the discolored zones appears similar to the unaffected seed coat — smooth and dry, not raised or sunken. The discoloration is distributed unevenly across the seed surface, often concentrated toward one side or the hilum area.
2. Black elongated hilum marks: Visible on many of the seeds as small (~1–2 mm), elongated, black oval structures — these are the seed hilum (attachment point), which appears dark black to dark gray. This is present on both apparently normal and discolored seeds.
3. One seed near the center has a small white, slightly irregular, dry, flaky patch (~1–2 mm) on its surface, located adjacent to the hilum area. It appears dry and slightly raised compared to the surrounding seed coat.
4. Seed color variation: Seeds range from uniform pale yellow-tan (normal-appearing) to heavily mottled or almost entirely covered in purple pigmentation. The variation is distributed randomly across the group — some seeds show no purple at all, others are mostly covered.
vision_features.absences: 1. No visible powdery or dusty coating on the seed surfaces. 2. No shriveling, wrinkling, or collapse of the seed shape — all seeds appear fully rounded and plump. 3. No visible thread-like growths, fuzzy textures, or filamentous structures on any seed surface. 4. No cracking, splitting, or breaking of the seed coat is visible on any of the seeds.
vision_features.summary: Approximately half of the roughly 13 soybean seeds held in a human palm display irregular patches of deep purple to violet-blue discoloration on their seed coats, while the remaining seeds appear uniform pale yellow-tan. The discoloration varies widely in extent — from small blotches to nearly full seed coverage — and has diffuse, blending edges with no distinct border or halo. All seeds retain their normal rounded, plump shape with smooth, dry surfaces. The most striking visual feature is the strong, deep purple pigmentation on the seed coats of the affected seeds, contrasting sharply with the yellow-tan base color of unaffected seeds.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Purple_Seed_Stain':
────────────────────────────────────────
Seeds may be symptomless or have pink to purple spots extending from the hilum. Crop value may be lowered by dockage or seed certification denial, but yield is not reduced.. Pink to purple spots extending from the hilum on the seed coat; seeds may also be completely symptomless.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus':
────────────────────────────────────────
Virus infection causes diffusion of pigments from the seed hilum, resulting in mottling of the seed coat. Hilum color determines the color and intensity of seed coat discoloration.. Mottling of the seed coat due to pigment diffusion from the hilum; color and intensity of discoloration is determined by hilum color. Mottling is associated with poor germination.
────────────────────────────────────────

DISCRIMINATING: 'Purple_Seed_Stain' vs 'Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus'
Ruling feature : Pattern of discoloration: discrete pink-to-purple spots radiating from the hilum (A) vs. diffuse mottling/bleeding of pigment across the seed coat (B)
Purple_Seed_Stain: Pink to purple spots that extend from the hilum in a defined spot pattern; seeds may alternatively appear completely symptomless with no discoloration.
Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus: Diffuse mottling of the seed coat caused by pigment diffusion spreading from the hilum; the color and intensity vary with hilum color, producing a blended, irregular pattern rather than discrete spots.
Decision rule  : IF the seed shows distinct, bounded pink-to-purple spots originating at the hilum (or is symptomless), classify as Purple Seed Stain (A); IF the seed shows diffuse, blended mottling/bleeding of color across the seed coat from the hilum, classify as Bean Pod Mottle Virus (B).
